page.stats.sub: How punctual the trains at Gara de Nord are: first the problems that stand out in the data (with N, raw figures and a link to the train, station or day), then what works well and the detail charts. The delay is the one read from the București Nord board; arrivals and departures are always kept separate.
page.rankings.title: Rankings

ui.donut.title: On time, late and over 30 min — {label}
ui.donut.desc.one: Of {n} trip completed with a delay reading: {ok} on time (at most {max} min), {late} late up to 30 min, {over} over 30 min.
ui.donut.desc.few: Of {n} trips completed with a delay reading: {ok} on time (at most {max} min), {late} late up to 30 min, {over} over 30 min.
ui.donut.desc.other: Of {n} trips completed with a delay reading: {ok} on time (at most {max} min), {late} late up to 30 min, {over} over 30 min.
charts.cal.desc: Calendar: one square per service day, coloured by the mean delay read; grey squares have a small sample.
charts.cal.foot: Every day appears in the table ({n} rows); percentages are missing below {min} journeys.
charts.cal.how: each square is a service day, in columns of one week each (Monday at the top, Sunday at the bottom); the darker the colour, the higher the mean delay read that day. Grey squares have fewer than {min} journeys with a delay read; outlined ones have journeys but no delay read; empty ones have no journey.
charts.cal.title: What does each day look like?
charts.interactive: Interactive chart: with the keyboard, the arrow keys change the value, Esc closes.
charts.tool.copied: Link copied: the chart opens straight at its place.
charts.tool.copy: Copy the link to this chart
charts.tool.copy_failed: Could not copy the link. Copy it from the address bar.
charts.tool.full_aria: Open the chart full screen, with the table beside it
stats.ch.desc: How many runs had 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 and more delay changes.
stats.ch.how: the number of times the board changed the delay of a run (0 = no change read). Arrivals and departures are separate. Isolated readings that go back to the previous value are not counted.
stats.ch.title: How many changes does a run have
stats.ch.top_h: The runs with the most changes — {board}
stats.ch.top_t: The runs with the most changes, {board}
stats.chart.dist_desc: Number of journeys by range of delay read (minutes). Total N = {n}.
stats.cl.count: {elig} (number × board, with at least {min} journeys with a delay read) · {below} below the threshold · {explain}
stats.cl.hero_sub: N ≥ {min} journeys with a delay read
stats.cl.order: Order: “most delayed” by the mean delay read (then the median); “most punctual” by % on time (then the mean). N = finished journeys with the delay read on the board at București Nord.
stats.cl.warn: There are no trains yet with at least {min} journeys with a delay read for the chosen filters. {has} data, but below the threshold — we do not rank them, because such a small sample says nothing reliable.
stats.cov.cannot: What cannot be concluded yet: {trend}the effect of weather, line changes (the reader confuses digits like 5/6 or 3/8) and the “best operator” — operators run different routes (correlation, not causation).
stats.cov.days: · {days} of history{span}; trends need at least {n} days.
stats.cov.gaps: Pauses in reading the board (over {thr} min): {count}, {total} min in total; the longest: {when} ({min} min). Trains during pauses may be missing.
stats.cov.no_gaps: No pause longer than {thr} min in reading the board.
stats.cov.results: Results: {done}, of which {unc} unconfirmed and {unk} with an unknown delay (not 0, not counted); {prog} still on the board.
stats.cov.title: Data coverage: {level}
stats.cov.trend: the trend from one day to the next,
stats.dim.desc: Mean delay read on the board at București Nord, with N journeys for each bar.
stats.dim.note: Bar = mean delay read (minutes); under each bar: N journeys. Faded bars have a small sample (N < {min}).
stats.dw.foot: Groups with at least {min} services are shown{omitted}. Durations that are negative or over 24 hours (reading pauses) are excluded.
stats.dw.how: the time between the first and the last time the train was seen on the board, for trains that have already disappeared. The median is the “middle” duration (half stay less); the mean is pulled up by the very long cases, which is why we show both.
stats.dw.loading: Loading the time on the board…
stats.dw.none: There are no finished trains yet for the chosen filters.
stats.dw.omitted: ({n} stations with fewer do not appear)
stats.dw.t_board: Time on the board, arrivals and departures
stats.dw.t_station: Time on the board by station
stats.dw.t_type: Time on the board by train type
stats.dw.title: How long does a train stay on the board?
stats.empty.no_journeys_filters: No journey for the chosen filters.
stats.empty.none: There is no data yet for the chosen filters. Try “All history” or another operator.
stats.empty.title: No journey to show
stats.err.noreply: The server did not respond. Try again in a moment.
stats.err.offline: You are offline — the statistics need a connection.
stats.err.rate: Too many requests — wait a few seconds.
stats.explain: “On time” = delay read ≤ {max} min · minimum sample {min} journeys{conf}{board}{period}
stats.fig.big: How often do very large delays occur?
stats.fig.big.head: {board}: {o30} over 30 min, {o60} over 60 min (N = {n})
stats.fig.big.how: the number of journeys over 30 and over 60 minutes and the largest cases. “Unconfirmed” = the train disappeared from the board before the estimated time, so the figure is indicative.
stats.fig.compare: Arrivals and departures, head to head
stats.fig.compare.foot: N = finished journeys with a delay read; “on time” ≤ {max} min.
stats.fig.compare.how: the same measures on the two boards. For arrivals the delay built up on the way; for departures the board shows the delay announced before departure, not the real time.
stats.fig.compare.mix: {board}: {station} pulls the figure {dir} ({a} of {n} on time, {pct}); without it: {ra} of {rn} ({rpct}).
stats.fig.daily: How has punctuality changed from one day to the next?
stats.fig.daily.desc: Percentage of journeys on time for each service day.
stats.fig.daily.how: each point is the percentage of journeys on time (≤ {max} min) in a service day. Days with too few journeys (N < {min}) have no percentage and are missing from the line. The strip shows N per day. Dotted line: the period mean.
stats.fig.daily.no_day: No day with data for the chosen filters.
stats.fig.daily.nstrip_desc: Journeys with a delay read per day.
stats.fig.daily.one_day: Only one day with data — the trend appears from the second day.
stats.fig.distribution.desc: Columns grouped by delay range, for {boards}.
stats.fig.distribution.how_n: each column shows how many of the finished journeys with a delay read had their delay in the range of minutes below it.
stats.fig.distribution.how_pct: each column shows what percentage of the finished journeys with a delay read had their delay in the range of minutes below it.
stats.fig.distribution.on_time5: The first two ranges (0 and 1–5 min) mean “on time”.
stats.fig.distribution.on_timeN: “On time” currently means at most {max} min.
stats.fig.growth: Does the delay grow after the first announcement?
stats.fig.growth.bars: First delay announced versus the final one — {board}
stats.fig.growth.bars_desc: How many grew, stayed the same or decreased after the first announcement.
stats.fig.growth.how: for journeys where the board showed a delay at some point (over 0): we compare the first value shown with the final one. Confirmed readings only; misreadings (e.g. “+” read as “4”) are removed.
stats.fig.heatmap: Which days and hours are the most problematic?
stats.fig.heatmap.desc: Heat map: 7 days × 24 hours; cells with a small sample are grey.
stats.fig.heatmap.how: each square is an hour (horizontally) of a weekday (vertically); the darker the colour, the higher the mean delay read. Grey squares have fewer than {min} journeys (too few for a conclusion); outlined ones have journeys but no delay read; empty ones have no journey. For exact figures, hover over a square or open the table below.
stats.fig.heatmap.only_cells: Only cells with at least one journey appear in the table ({n}).
stats.fig.heatmap.short_history: Short history ({days}): each weekday currently has at most one calendar date, so the map shows specific days, not yet a weekly pattern.
stats.fig.heatmap.title: Mean delay by hour and day — {board}
stats.fig.hourly: At what hour are trains the most late?
stats.fig.hourly.desc: Median delay read for each hour of the day, per board.
stats.fig.hourly.how: the horizontal axis is the scheduled hour (00–23); the dot shows the median delay read for the trains of that hour — half of them were less late, half more. Hollow circles have too few journeys: the figure is real but unreliable, and is not joined into the line. The strip below shows how many journeys (N) are behind each hour.
stats.fig.hourly.nstrip_desc: The number of journeys with a delay read in each hour.
stats.fig.operators: Which operators are the most punctual?
stats.fig.operators.how: each row is an operator, as written on the board; the bar shows what percentage of its journeys were on time. Operators with too few journeys appear without a bar, with N only.
stats.fig.platforms: Which lines (platforms) are used the most?
stats.fig.platforms.desc: Grouped columns: how many arrivals and departures used each line.
stats.fig.platforms.how: how many journeys each line had, by the last line read on the board. Journeys with no line read are counted separately (“line not read”), not as line 0.
stats.fig.platforms.none: No line read for the chosen filters.
stats.fig.problems.how: What stands out in the delays read on the board, ranked by severity × how many journeys it affects × confidence in the figures. Deterministic calculation from the data (no AI). “On time” = at most {max} min; groups are compared by median, not by mean; below {min} journeys no percentages appear.
stats.fig.problems.none: No clear problem in the filtered data.
stats.fig.proutes: Which directions have the most delays?
stats.fig.proutes.foot: {elig} comparable directions · {single} with a single train · {below} with fewer than {min} journeys (not enough data).
stats.fig.proutes.how: the origin station (arrivals) or destination station (departures), ordered by median. Only those with at least {min} journeys and at least 2 different trains are included (otherwise it would be a single train, not a direction).
stats.fig.proutes.insufficient: Not enough data: no direction with enough journeys.
stats.fig.proutes.none: No direction with a median over {max} min.
stats.fig.quality.block_desc: {title}: counts and shares of the total.
stats.fig.quality.block_desc2: {title}: counts and percentages of the total.
stats.fig.quality.excluded: Excluded from all statistics{scope}: {ghost} (rows read wrongly, with no real train) and {low} journeys from the reduced-quality period (the first hours of operation, with the old reader). {unc} journeys have the station or operator name read uncertainly.
stats.fig.quality.how: how many journeys have a certain result and how successful the automatic (OCR) readings of the board were. Only finished journeys with a delay read count towards the statistics; “unknown” does not mean 0.
stats.fig.recurrent: Which trains are late day after day?
stats.fig.recurrent.foot: Showing {shown} of {count} late every day; {o15} exceeded 15 min every day; {seen} on at least {days} days.
stats.fig.recurrent.how: a train is listed here if it was seen on at least {days} days and was late (over {max} min) on each of them (from 5 days, one may be missing). For a train we only have a few days, so we show raw figures per day, not percentages.
stats.fig.recurrent.none: No train late on all the days it was seen ({seen} on at least {days} days).
stats.fig.recurrent.stat: late on {late} of {days} days · {o15} over 15 min · median {median} · maximum {max}
stats.fig.routes: Which routes are the latest — and which are the most punctual?
stats.fig.routes.below: {n} below the threshold are not ranked.
stats.fig.routes.full: Full ranking of trains and stations →
stats.fig.routes.how: the station is the origin of the train (for arrivals) or its destination (for departures), as shown on the board. The delay is still the one read at București Nord, not at the station. Only stations with at least {min} journeys with a delay read are included; the late ones are ordered by median (a single extreme case does not move the ranking). Tap a station for its page.
stats.fig.routes.no_station: No station with N ≥ {min} yet ({has} data below the threshold).
stats.fig.routes.table: Routes: the most delayed and the most punctual
stats.fig.share.how: each slice is the share of one category among the observed journeys (with or without a delay read): first arrivals versus departures, then by train type and by operator. Hover or use the keyboard over a slice or the legend to see the figures; the colour is repeated in the legend together with the name and a pattern (lines, dots, hatching). Below {min} journeys we show raw figures only, no percentages.
stats.fig.traffic: When is the station the busiest?
stats.fig.traffic.chart: Journeys scheduled per hour (mean per day)
stats.fig.traffic.desc: Grouped columns: arrivals and departures scheduled in each hour, mean per day.
stats.fig.traffic.how: how many journeys are scheduled in each hour, on average over a day with data ({days}). All observed journeys are counted, with or without a delay read.
stats.fig.trend: Is it getting better or worse?
stats.fig.trend.dir: {board}: {label} ({sign}{diff} percentage points on time, second half versus first)
stats.fig.trend.few: {board}: too few complete days for a comparison
stats.fig.trend.foot: Below {min} journeys per day: no percentage.
stats.fig.trend.how: punctuality for each service day. A trend is drawn only with at least {n} days of history; partial days (the current day, excluded hours, long reading pauses) are not part of the comparison.
stats.fig.trend.insufficient: Not enough history: {days} of {n} days. We do not draw a conclusion about an increase or decrease yet — below are only the raw figures per day.
stats.fig.types: Which train types are more punctual?
stats.fig.types.how: R = Regio, RM = Regio Metropolitan, RE = Regio Expres, IR = InterRegio, IRN = InterRegio night train, IC = InterCity (the type shown on the board). Bar = percentage on time; no bar = small sample.
stats.fig.weather.bars_desc: Mean delay read by weather group.
stats.fig.weather.collecting: The weather analysis is still being gathered.
stats.fig.weather.collecting_b: {matched} already have weather attached, in {days} ({obs}). The charts appear after at least {needed} days and a minimum of two groups with N ≥ {min} — otherwise the differences would depend more on the hour of day than on the weather.
stats.fig.weather.foot: Arrivals and departures are analysed separately; {matched} with weather attached, in {days}.
stats.fig.weather.how: compares the delay read across weather groups (Open-Meteo model, ±30 min around the scheduled time). It shows an association only.
stats.fig.windows: At what hours and on which days do delays pile up?
stats.fig.windows.bars_desc: Percentage of journeys over 15 min, by scheduled-hour window; no bar = small sample.
stats.fig.windows.how: each bar is a 3-hour window (scheduled time) and shows what percentage of journeys were late by more than 15 min. “Critical” = well above the rest of the board and on at least 2 different days. An “episode” is a single day with many delays over 30 min — an incident, not a pattern.
stats.fig.windows.no_episode: No episode (a day with at least 3 delays over 30 min in a 3-hour window, twice the usual rate).
stats.fig.windows.tip: {o15} of {n} over 15 min{crit}, on {late} of {days} days
stats.gl.confirmed.d: The train disappeared from the board after the estimated time (scheduled + delay), and the delay had been read at most {gap} min before.
stats.gl.delay.d: The delay shown on the CFR board at București Nord, read automatically (OCR). It is not the real arrival or departure time, nor the delay at other stations.
stats.gl.ghost.d: A row misread by OCR that did not match a real train; excluded from everything.
stats.gl.journey.d: One appearance of a train on a board (arrivals or departures) on a service day. A train (number) usually has one journey per day.
stats.gl.median.d: Median: half of the journeys were less late. p90: 90% were at most this late.
stats.gl.n.d: The number of finished journeys with a delay read behind a figure.
stats.gl.ontime.d: Delay read of at most {max} minutes.
stats.gl.small.d: Below {min} journeys: we show raw figures only (mean, median, maximum), no percentages.
stats.gl.title: Glossary
stats.gl.tjo.d: Train = the train number; journey = the train on a given day; observation = one reading of the board (every few tens of seconds), so a journey has many observations.
stats.gl.unconfirmed.d: We have a delay read, but the disappearance was not observed at the right time (e.g. the reading of the board was interrupted). It counts towards the statistics unless you tick “Confirmed results only”.
stats.gl.unknown.d: The delay was never read. It is not treated as 0 and does not count towards the statistics.
stats.hero.on_time_sub: {ok} of {n} journeys with a delay read (≤ {max} min)
stats.jr.note: Newest first{only} (without the period filter). Tap a journey for the result, the reason and the readings chart.
stats.jr.title: Latest journeys
stats.jr.uncertain: The station/operator name was read uncertainly
stats.kpi.line: {ok} of {n} finished journeys with a delay read (N = {n}) · {obs}
stats.kpi.none: no journey with a delay read
stats.kpi.small: small sample: the percentage is not shown
stats.part.charts_sub: All the figures, by question: distribution, days, hours, operators, routes, lines, weather and data quality.
stats.part.details_sub: The trains, hours, days and directions behind the list above.
stats.pc.few: Little data (N = {n}, changes = {c}): the figures are indicative and may change a lot as history accumulates.
stats.pc.foot: The platform is read from the București Nord board; a change can also be a correction of an uncertain reading ({n} values ignored).
stats.pc.how: a train is “changed” when the board showed at least two different platforms for it (for example 6 then 4). Only services with a platform read are counted; values that are not a real platform (1–{max}) are misreadings and are ignored.
stats.pc.line: {a} of {n} services with a platform changed their platform{pct}
stats.pc.none: There are no services with a platform read yet for the chosen filters.
stats.pc.title: Platforms changed after the announcement
stats.q.title: Delay read for {dk} of {fin} finished journeys; {c} with a confirmed result.
stats.qd.conf_note: The percentage = confirmed out of the finished journeys (those in progress have no result yet). The current day and the first day with data are partial.
stats.qd.cov_note: Hours 0–23, left to right; each cell = the successful captures out of the {n} expected.
stats.qd.gap_cap: Hours with coverage below the threshold
stats.qd.no_cap: There are no captures in the chosen period.
stats.qd.no_gaps: There are no gaps in the chosen period.
stats.qd.no_j: There are no journeys in the chosen period.
stats.qd.no_obs: There are no observations in the chosen period.
stats.qd.s1i: How many journeys had a final result confirmed, unconfirmed, in progress or unknown, per day.
stats.qd.s2i: The rows read from the board, after validation: ok, uncertain, incomplete, rejected.
stats.qd.s3i: Successful captures compared with the expected ones (60 per hour); gaps are highlighted.
stats.quality.line: Data quality: {j}, {fin} finished; delay read for {dk} ({pct} of the finished ones); results: {c} confirmed, {u} unconfirmed, {k} unknown, {p} in progress.
stats.ranked.desc: Percentage on time by {what}; rows without a bar have a small sample.
stats.ranked.foot: Bar = % on time (≤ {max} min), only with N ≥ {min}. No bar = small sample, raw figures in the table.
stats.ranked.tip_small: N = {n} (too few for a percentage), mean {mean}
stats.rl.not_elig: not eligible for the chosen filters.
stats.rl.pos: Place {pos} of {of} stations ({board}) with ≥ {min} journeys with a delay read · place 1 = the most delayed.
stats.rs.count: {elig} (station × board, with at least {min} journeys with a delay read) · {below} below the threshold
stats.rs.note: Station = the origin (for arrivals) or the destination (for departures) shown on the board. The delay is the one read on the board at București Nord, not the one at the station. Arrivals and departures are ranked separately (the “Board” column).
stats.rs.title: Station ranking
stats.rs.warn: There are no stations yet with at least {min} journeys with a delay read for the chosen filters. {has} data, but below the threshold — we do not rank them.
stats.sample.none: No finished journey with a delay read (N = 0): there are no statistics for this group.
stats.sample.small: Small sample (N = {n} < {min}): percentages are not shown.
stats.share.arr_dep_title: Arrivals and departures: share of journeys
stats.sl.card_sub: the share of each board in all the journeys in the list
stats.sl.hero_on_board: on the board at Gara de Nord
stats.sl.limit: Showing the first {n} stations — narrow the search.
stats.sl.none: There is no data yet for stations.
stats.sl.note: Station = the origin (for arrivals) or the destination (for departures) shown on the board at Gara de Nord. The delays on the station pages are the ones read at București Nord, not at the station. “Uncertain name” = the name was only read uncertainly (OCR) on the board.
stats.sn.heading: Station {name}
stats.sn.not_seen: The station was not observed on the board{name}.
stats.sn.title: Station {name} · Tabela Gara de Nord
stats.sn.uncertain: {n} the station or operator name read uncertainly (OCR).
stats.sn.warn_b: The delay is the one shown on the board at București Nord, not at the station.
stats.stp.final: Of the final delay (runs with a delay at the end, N = {n}): {share}; {complete} runs had the final value from the start, {later} received minutes later{added}.
stats.stp.how: the board raises the delay step by step (e.g. 0 → 5 → 10 min). We count the jumps between two values read one after the other, from the previous value (initially 0) to the new one. Decreases are shown separately; a value that appears for a single reading and goes back exactly to the previous one (A → B → A) is reading noise and is not counted.
stats.stp.none: No change of the delay read.
stats.stp.share_min: {a} of {b} min announced at the first appearance
stats.stp.share_pct: {v}% was already announced at the first appearance
stats.stp.title: How the delay grows, in steps
stats.stp.top_desc: The number of transitions from one delay value to another.
stats.stp.typical: Typical step: {size} · median time between two changes: {gap}{pairs} · {up}, {down}{downmed}.
stats.summary.coverage: Period: {period} · {journeys} ({trains}) · {obs} · excluded: {ghost}, {low} from the reduced-quality period
stats.summary.generated: Computed at {time} · recomputed at most once every {ttl} s · “on time” = delay read ≤ {max} min · minimum sample {min} journeys
stats.summary.insufficient_b: The figures below are real (read from the board), but trends by hour, day and operator only become reliable after at least {n} days; they will change as data accumulates.
stats.summary.insufficient_h: Not enough data yet — {days} of history.
stats.summary.title: In brief
stats.t.heading: Train {name}
stats.t.invalid: Invalid train number. Pick a train from the train list.
stats.t.journeys_note: Newest first. Service date = the day of the scheduled time. Tap a journey for the result, the reason and the readings chart.
stats.t.notfound: The train was not observed on the board (for the chosen filters).
stats.t.spark_note: Delay per journey, from the oldest to the newest (min)
stats.t.title: Train {name} · Tabela Gara de Nord
stats.tr.none: There is no data yet for trains.
stats.tr.note: Journey = one appearance of the train on a board on a service day; a train number can have several journeys. N = the finished journeys with the delay read (only they count towards the statistics).
stats.tr.same_scale: The same scale across the whole table
stats.tr.small: {a} of {n} rows have a small sample (N < {min}): percentages are not shown there (“—”).
stats.trend.few: Fewer than 2 days with a delay read
stats.trend.text: Mean delay per day, last {days} days (up to {last}): {list}
stats.warn.small_pct: Small sample (N = {n} < {min}): percentages are not shown.
stats.warn.small_raw: Small sample (N = {n} < {min}): raw figures only, no percentages.
stats.wk.foot: Weeks accumulated: {w}. Days with fewer than {n} appearances stay marked “not enough data”; arrivals and departures are not mixed.
stats.wk.how: each row is a day of the week; services are all the trains scheduled on that day, and the percentage on time, the median delay and the share over 30 minutes are computed only from the delays read. A day is compared only after {n} distinct appearances (finished calendar days); until then it shows “not enough data”. Today does not count, because it has not ended.
stats.wk.pending: The comparison will become valid after ~4 weeks of data
stats.wk.title: How do the days of the week compare?
stats.wk.weeks: Weeks accumulated: {w} of {n} needed (the best-covered day of the week).
